translation_notes: prefixes: CMSO->cmso, LDO->ldo, PLDO->pldo, PODO->podo, CDCO->cdco, PROV->prov, ASMO->asmo

Twelve selectors, all single-pattern m{ } ... .first(): next((s for s,_,_ in graph.triples((None, P, activity))), None) is `.first()` (it has a default, so first-or-None, not next(iter(...))) and each graph.value(s, p) is `.first()`. The three component reads x/y/z of one vector/normal vector are independent reads fed by one outer node and stay three separate m{ } (fused as one join they would drop the whole vector instead of raising AttributeError on a missing component); plane -> normal vector -> distance are optional hops guarded by `is not None`, and the `for vec in ...: ... break` is kept as written. No true conjunctive chain here (ldpy/016): the stratum has no multi-pattern m{ }.
Namespaces come from the project (atomrdf.namespace), so `from atomrdf_context import cmso:, prov:` replaces the seven @prefix of the draft (only CMSO and PROV are used by the region).

Context shim atomrdf_context.py: real namespace IRIs and get_sample_object verbatim from atomrdf 0.12.3 (atomrdf not installed); Shear is a keyword-only stand-in for the pydantic model; `classmethod` is shadowed by the identity because the region is extracted from a class body and a bare module-level classmethod object is not callable. original.py edited only to point its two imports at the shim and to import that classmethod; translated.ldpy has the same imports.

Not covered, by construction: activity_id=None. rdflib reads None as a wildcard in graph.triples/objects (and graph.value(None, p) returns None as two terms are unbound), whereas an interpolated None raises TypeError in m{ } (ldpy.ANY would restore the wildcard for triples/objects but not for value()). The repository never passes None (the id comes from the graph), so the fixture does not test it.

Driver: 10 calls: seven activities of the fixture (complete; no derivedFrom/vector/normal vector; nothing at all; normal vector without distance; missing component -> AttributeError on both sides, vector and normal vector; two vectors and two output samples for one activity), a str id, an unknown activity, an empty graph. Neighbours with the predicates reversed or on another activity must not match. Verified by mutation (wasGeneratedBy -> wasDerivedFrom, an extra join pattern on distance): check FAILS.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the six component reads x/y/z of the shear vector and of the normal vector become one local helper `components(vector)`, a comprehension over "xyz" with `CMSO[f"hasComponent_{axis}"]` (a missing component still raises AttributeError, now before the next component is read, with no other effect); the `for vec in ...: ...; break` loop becomes `next(graph.objects(...), None)` and a conditional expression; the generator over graph.triples() becomes `next(graph.subjects(PROV.wasGeneratedBy, activity), None)`; `normal_vector = distance = None` on one line. Kept: the `if output_sample` and the two `is not None` guards. graph.value(None, P, activity) was rejected: with activity_id=None it returns None where the original's triples() treats None as a wildcard.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: only the namespace terms change, `PROV.x`/`CMSO.x` becoming prefixed names and `CMSO[f"hasComponent_{axis}"]` becoming `cmso:hasComponent_{axis}`. A `m{ }(graph).first()` for either `next(...)` read measured the same 223 tokens, a full `@graph graph` + m{ } version 230: the Python reads are kept, being no longer and exact on activity_id=None, where an interpolated None raises in m{ }. No island is left; no exception to the symmetry rule.
Most of the notation gain is the header's: the original imports eight names from the namespace module, the translation two prefixes (see the header variant).
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: LDO, PLDO, PODO, CDCO, Literal and ASMO are unused and go; the two shim imports become `from atomrdf_context import get_sample_object, classmethod, CMSO, PROV`.
optimized_header.ldpy: nothing unused (get_sample_object, classmethod, cmso: and prov: are all used): a copy of optimized.ldpy.
